BUILT (proposal/dial-cancel.md). Door (a): `dial_with_backoff` honours the ambient `CancelSignal` - the socket open's abort listener closes the half-open WebSocket (handlers unhooked first) and the dial answers `DialFailure::Cancelled` -> `RpcError::Cancelled` / `connect_socket*`'s sentence; the backoff sleep's abort ENDS the dial; an abort after the open leaves the duplex `Connected`. The signal is a PARAMETER of `dial_with_backoff` (`dial_attempt`): `handle_drop`'s redial passes `None`, because the socket-event closures capture the connect's nursery as ambient and a redial reading it after a race's cancel ended at once and closed the duplex for good (plant-proven; its own pin). Door (b): `std::rpc::dial_within(ms: i32, dial)` over `nursery` + `Timer` + `Task::race` - a timer win cancels the nursery and answers `Err(RpcError::Timeout)`; a dial win calls off only the timer (nothing of the new connection cancelled). Two NEW `RpcError` arms, `Timeout` + `Cancelled`: the one exhaustive match in the estate was std's `status_of_outcome` (504 / 500); kolt's client.vl:151 and service_layer.rs match with a fallthrough - no kolt patch. Native: there is NO native WebSocket dial (F1 S1b refuses the host type), so the cancel arms are JS-only; `dial_within` is plain std code and runs natively over any dial (differential incl. a minute-long dial cut at 20 ms). Pins dial_cancel.rs (6, harness-ordered through stdin and held listeners, no sleeps; plants: the throwing backoff sleep, no close() on abort, no detach, the redial reading the ambient), `native_differential::a179_*`; §4.4 is an outcome pin.
